transitions.summary: The continuous position lock gained an exception: v1 reads 'monsters on your opponent's side of the field cannot change their battle positions, except with a card effect', where v0 imposes it without qualification. No upstream implementation exists for this text - both the goat variant and the pre-errata variant register a plain EFFECT_CANNOT_CHANGE_POSITION with EFFECT_FLAG_SET_AVAILABLE and no card-effect carve-out - so this intermediate version has no reproducible implementation.

transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the flip is narrowed to 'all monsters your opponent controlled when this card was activated' and to monsters that can actually be turned face-down. The goat script flips Duel.GetMatchingGroup(nil,tp,0,LOCATION_MZONE,nil) at resolution - every opponent monster, with no Card.IsCanTurnSet filter, so Tokens and other monsters that cannot be Set are caught and end up in face-up Defense Position, which upstream annotates as 'Affects tokens as well, they're changed to faceup defense'. The pre-errata script adds Duel.SetTargetCard(g) at activation over the IsCanTurnSet group and flips only g:Filter(Card.IsRelateToEffect,...) at resolution, so the affected set is snapshotted at activation and unsettable monsters are excluded.

rulings_check.difference: c2 (2012): monsters that cannot be turned face-down (Monster Tokens, which are always face-up) are left alone; in the era they are simply changed to Defense Position. Modern script flips only monsters that can be turned face-down. Which monsters are flipped: the era/goat card flips those on the opponent's field when the card resolves (so a monster Special Summoned in response is flipped); c2 (2012) snapshots the monsters controlled at activation; c3 (2017) returns to resolution-time. Only c2 is a difference between the era and a later version, c3 undoes it.

review.notes:
Two upstream codes exist and they implement DIFFERENT historical versions, so they are not folded: goat 504700018 matches lineage v0 (FET-EN042, 2005-03-01) exactly and is the baseline; pre-errata 511003008 implements v3 (its cdb text is a 0.9639 active-voice paraphrase of LCYW-EN281 - 'Change all monsters your opponent controlled when this card was activated to face-down Defense Position' vs the lineage's passive 'are changed to') and is attached to change 3. Both target eras resolve cleanly: GOAT (2005-04-01) precedes the v1 window and takes the baseline; Edison (2010-04-24) falls in 2006-11-25 .. 2012-09-29 and takes change 2's goat implementation. The v1 excursion is recorded rather than smoothed because it is a real printed behavioural clause dated by two printings in the packet, but it is unimplemented by anyone - hence the implementation-gap flag and the deliberately fail-safe BLOCKED interval for any snapshot inside 2005-11-02 .. 2006-11-25. Change 2 reuses the baseline passcode as its resulting_implementation because v2's behaviour is v0's behaviour; that is intentional, not a duplication. Observation, not a change: lineage v5 (RA05-EN059, Rarity Collection 5, 2026-04-09) is newer than the pinned cards.cdb text and rewrites the flip again as 'When this card is activated: If your opponent controls a face-up monster, flip all monsters they control to face-down Defense Position'; the pinned modern text matches v4 exactly, so the record stops at v4 and the RA05 printing is left for a later refresh. Remaining diff items across both variants - CATEGORY_SET on the modern activate, the SetOperationInfo hint parameters, EVENT_PHASE|PHASE_STANDBY vs '+', the reset spelling and Duel.IsTurnPlayer(tp) vs GetTurnPlayer()==tp - are hint-only or identical; the 2nd-Standby-Phase self-destruction is the same turn-counter routine in all three scripts.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Swords of Concealing Light). The rulings read support d1 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [c2] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu. [c3] d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.
